title: Vintage Gibson J-200 Value Guide: Prices Through 1979
description: Compare vintage Gibson J-200 values from 1947 to 1979, with prices by era, original bridges, condition notes and photos of guitars from my archive.
alt: Sunburst SJ-200 with floral pickguard and open moustache bridge in a pink-lined case

faqs.q: How Much Is A 1950s Gibson J-200 Worth?
faqs.a: A standard 1950 to 1959 J-200 has a guide range of $12,750 to $17,800 in all-original excellent condition with its original case. Repairs, changes and substantial wear need a separate appraisal. The range isn't a guaranteed offer.

faqs.q: What Is A 1970s J-200 Artist Worth?
faqs.a: The 1970 to 1979 range is $3,550 to $5,800 in all-original excellent condition with the original case. Altered and repaired guitars may fall below it. I confirm the exact model and condition before applying the table.

faqs.q: Why Is There No Prewar Price Band?
faqs.a: Prewar examples need individual appraisals because their construction, condition and documented history can put them in a different market from postwar J-200s. They aren't included in the postwar ranges.

No. In SJ-200, SJ identifies the Super Jumbo family. Gibson's Southern Jumbo is a different model. I wouldn't apply this table to a Southern Jumbo merely because a label or description uses the initials SJ.

faqs.q: Does A Converted Saddle Increase Value?
faqs.a: A conversion may suit a player's preferences, but it changes the comparison with an original collector example. I need to know what was changed, what remains inside the guitar and whether the removed parts survive. There isn't a fixed premium for a conversion.

faqs.q: Does A Quality Refret Remove All-Original Status?
faqs.a: A quality refret preserves the all-original classification of an otherwise original guitar and removes museum-quality status. Neck reshaping, refinishing and structural repairs are separate conditions.
No. These are guide ranges for guitars in stated condition. An actual offer depends on the instrument and sale terms, and selling costs can affect the owner's proceeds.
